title: Atmosphere, Insolation and Heat Budget

cards.b: Monsoon, deserts, cyclones and global warming all start with one question: how much solar energy reaches a place, and where does it go? The heat budget is the answer and a UPSC favourite.

Dry air by volume: nitrogen 78%, oxygen 21%, argon 0.93%, carbon dioxide about 0.04% (over 420 ppm as of the mid-2020s, rising). Water vapour varies from 0 to 4%. Dust, salt and pollen act as hygroscopic nuclei for cloud formation.

Gases are held by gravity. About 99% of air lies within 32 km of the ground.

Boundaries are called pauses: tropopause, stratopause and so on. The tropopause is higher at the equator (about 18 km) than at the poles (about 8 km). Weather happens only in the troposphere. The ozone layer sits at 15 to 35 km.

Insolation is incoming solar radiation, mostly short-wave. It depends on: the angle of rays (equator gets near-vertical rays), length of day, the transparency of air (clouds, dust), and the Sun-Earth distance.

Earth is nearest the Sun (perihelion) in early January and farthest (aphelion) in early July. Season, not distance, makes summer and winter, because Earth's axis is tilted by 23.5 degrees.
Earth neither heats up nor cools down overall, so incoming and outgoing energy balance. Greenhouse gases keep the average surface near 15 C instead of about -18 C.

Conduction: contact, mostly at the ground. Convection: vertical air currents. Advection: horizontal movement, which is more important in weather, e.g. the hot dry Loo of north India. Latent heat: heat released when vapour condenses, which fuels cyclones.
Inversions form on long, clear, calm winter nights with snow cover. They trap smoke in valleys. Mountain-side inversions favour orchards mid-slope because cold air drains downhill.

The natural effect is useful. Human burning of fossil fuels adds CO2 and methane, thickening the blanket. The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to hold warming well below 2 C and pursue 1.5 C. Critics note that India, with low per capita emissions, argues for common but differentiated responsibilities.

Ozone depletion is a separate problem: the Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out CFCs; the Kigali Amendment (2016) phases down HFCs.

The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight states (Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram). The Loo, pre-monsoon heat waves (IMD flags them above 40 C in plains) and Delhi winter smog from inversions and stubble burning all follow from this lesson.

The Indo-Gangetic Plain is one of the world's most polluted air basins.

Likely questions

"Explain the heat budget of the Earth." (10 marks)

"What is temperature inversion? Discuss its effects." (10 marks)

Structure: define; draw the 100-unit diagram; explain the balance; link to greenhouse warming; give an Indian example.

Prelims tip: ozone is in the stratosphere; the ionosphere reflects radio waves; the tropopause is highest at the equator; albedo is 35%.
